report: The patient's recurrent shin ulcer that temporarily healed with antibiotics but relapsed, together with chronic inflammatory infiltrate and absence of osteomyelitis, supports a chronic bacterial ulcer (Staphylococcus/Streptococcus pyoderma). Intact sensation, non-thickened nerves, and failure of anti-tubercular and leprosy therapy argue against tuberculous/leprotic ulcer. Normal systemic work-up and antibiotic response make infection more likely than autoimmune ulcer, though autoimmune serology and DIF are still needed to fully exclude it. The frontier has been refined to chronic bacterial ulcer with confidence 0.70; confirmatory wound culture, 16S PCR, and special stains are required.
